the number of Langerhns cells is increased and the number of CD4+ T cells is increased in oral lichen plans, but the number of CD8+ T cells is decreased.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LCs and T cell subsets play an important role in the pathogenesis and progression of LP.
the pathogenesis of oral lichen planos is not a single mechanism but rather a multifactorial process.
the pathogenesis of oral LP involves an immunological process in which LCs play an important role in initiating immune responses, and OKT4-positive T cells may be involved in the pathogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LP is an immunologically mediated disease, and that LCs play a key role, especially by stimulating T helper cells, in the pathogenesis.
the pathogenesis of oral LP is related to the immune response, and that LC is a key factor in initiating cell-mediated immune response.

LCs are more numerous in LP, and that the subepithelial inflammatory cell infiltrate of LP is composed mainly of OKT4 and OKT11 positive cells, which may play a role in the pathogenesis and progression of LP.

we have developed a new method for the preparation of the Langerhans Cells (LCs) and the T cell subsets in the oral mucosa.
the presence of LC in the oral mucosa is not sufficient to induce LP, but the number of LC is important in the pathogenesis.
